target_customer: K-12 teachers, schools and districts paying per student for leveled science and history reading
problem: Students in the same class read at different levels, so grade level science and social studies text is out of reach for many; teachers lack time to level content.
business_model: Per student SaaS subscription for schools, with a free month for teachers

founders.name: Brendan Finch
founders.background_notes: YC page and company site call him a veteran teacher who created the product from the classroom; a CB Insights profile reported seven years teaching science, not independently verified.

founders.name: Grenard Madrigal
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder and CTO on the YC page, no bio.

investors: Stanford Social Impact Venture Capital Fund

technical_complexity.rationale: Adaptive leveling uses quiz driven level changes and curated leveled content; the content creation workload is larger than the engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Leveled content libraries and standards alignment take effort but Newsela and others sold overlapping leveled nonfiction.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Newsela remained a larger leveled nonfiction provider while RocketLit stayed small and kept selling per student.

market_need_then: Schools were adopting NGSS science standards and reading level gaps were a known classroom problem; RocketLit says it served over 650,000 students by the YC listing.

identity.voice_and_tone: Born in the classroom, created by a teacher

branding.community_and_virality: Company site says it was featured in Forbes, The Huffington Post and The Daily Dot.

brand_strength.rationale: A literacy and rocket pun name with teacher founder story and some press mentions, but no independent evidence of brand pull.

outcome_analysis: RocketLit is a small teacher founded edtech company that sells leveled science and history reading per student. No substantial venture round was found and the company remains listed active with 11 people, so the story is a bootstrapped niche business rather than a venture scale outcome; the cause of limited growth is not public.
notes: Funding: CB Insights lists $120K over 2 rounds (Y Combinator and Stanford Social Impact Venture Capital Fund, Aug 2016) and a profile says family and friends money plus a NewSchools grant; a single aggregator so unverified and not recorded as rounds. A school data site says the product was formerly called BirdBrain; the name change was not confirmed from a primary source. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news found. Competitors: Newsela and ReadWorks exist but sources found are undated, so the list is empty. Outcome search returned nothing relevant. Completeness pass: CB Insights reports 120K over 2 rounds with the latest dated 2016-08-24; recorded as one combined entry (stage other) because no per-round split is given. Single database; a second search found no confirmation of the Stanford or NewSchools items.
